slot.brief: A source moving toward then away from a stationary observer; compare the observed frequencies in the two cases.

stem: A fixed microphone records a tone from a source moving first toward it and then away. If the ratio of the frequencies heard in these two cases is $3:2$ and the speed of sound is $350$ m s$^{-1}$, what is the source speed?

verdicts.working: For a moving source, the approaching-to-receding frequency ratio is (v+u)/(v-u)=3/2. Thus 2(v+u)=3(v-u), so u=v/5=70 m s⁻¹.

working:
$\dfrac{f_{\text{toward}}}{f_{\text{away}}}=\dfrac{v+u_s}{v-u_s}=\dfrac{3}{2}$
$2(v+u_s)=3(v-u_s)$
$5u_s=v$
$u_s=\dfrac{350}{5}=70\ \text{m s}^{-1}$

Independent check: For a moving source, the approaching-to-receding frequency ratio is (v+u)/(v-u)=3/2. Thus 2(v+u)=3(v-u), so u=v/5=70 m s⁻¹.
solution: For a moving source, $\dfrac{f_{\text{toward}}}{f_{\text{away}}}=\dfrac{v+u_s}{v-u_s}=\dfrac{3}{2}$. Thus $2(v+u_s)=3(v-u_s)$, giving $u_s=\dfrac{v}{5}=\dfrac{350}{5}=70\ \text{m s}^{-1}$.
